pure-announcement.rationale: It is vendor content-marketing shaped as a tutorial, not a launch, release note or funding announcement.

duplicate.rationale: The nearest concepts are all MCP/protocol notes; nothing existing covers desktop app licensing or distribution.

unfalsifiable.rationale: The central mechanisms — Rust-side validation, keychain storage, signed offline tokens, Tauri signing requirements — are checkable against the public SDK and linked Tauri docs, even if the piracy statistics are unsourced.

durability.rationale: The note is dominated by LicenseSeat config keys, SDK feature tables and prices ($99/year Apple, $300-600 EV certs) that churn, with only a few embedded principles (validate in the Rust layer, offline grace periods, sign or lose conversions) that age well.

actionability.rationale: Nearly every step is a product-only instruction for one vendor's SDK — install the plugin, paste the API key, call activate() — rather than transferable guidance for building licensing.

atomicity.rationale: Everything serves one statable idea — how to license and distribute a paid Tauri app with validation in the Rust layer — so the sub-steps are stages of a single workflow, not separate concepts.
